assessments.reasoning: The unsigned annotated SPDX v3.29.0 tag points to 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, matching the immutable no-RFN detail URL.

The exact licenseId, no-RFN name and two comment fields agree on absence. The copyright example omits an RFN, the heading gives 26 February 2007, and isDeprecatedLicenseId is false. The references to OFL_web and OSI carry match=false and N/A respectively.
The exact publisher text defines RFNs through names specified as such after copyright. Its general clause concerning RFNs can appear in the license even when a font has no designated name.

FAQ 5.6 expressly permits release without declaring an RFN. FAQ 5.7 confirms that the main font name carries no default reservation as of 1.1. Together they resolve the edition-specific applicability question at the documentary level.

challenge.method: Compared the 1.1 no-RFN comment, template and publisher definition against the unspecified 1.1 record and the problematic 1.0 no-RFN template. Tested the effect of an incomplete font notice.
challenge.results: The 1.1 definition permits a release with no designated names. The 1.0 template’s user-visible-name default does not carry over. An unknown or incomplete notice leaves RFN status undetermined and cannot substantiate the explicit absent choice for a font.

limitations: The absent value describes the SPDX choice. Determining absence in a font requires its actual notices. Text equivalence, installation and redistribution require separate evidence.
reasoning: The exact SPDX identifier is OFL-1.1-no-RFN. Its comment restricts it to cases with no RFN. The template’s sample copyright line omits a reservation, and SIL’s 1.1 definition and FAQ allow the author to declare none.
